summary: Temporary device-pool policy for interns & ephemeral service account lifecycle
description: Issue summary: HR has requested a formal policy for issuing 'floating' loaner laptops and peripheral kits to interns and short-term contractors. Background: Historically, teams have borrowed devices from a small centralized pool for interns (3-12 week stints). Two recent cases resulted in (a) a service account that was not rotated/disabled after device return and (b) a device reassigned without KMS rekeying. Impact: Risk of lingering credentials, unclear asset custody, and noncompliance with audit expectations for device lifecycle. Request: Draft a concise policy that covers (1) device assignment workflow, (2) mandatory asset-tagged checkout/in with timestamped ownership, (3) ephemeral service account creation tied to device tag with automatic expiry, (4) KMS key rewrap/rotation requirements on device reassignment, (5) minimum acceptable device wipe process and proof, and (6) exceptions process for urgent hires. Acceptance criteria: Policy documented in Confluence; one-runbook for IT to execute provisioning and deprovisioning; a small automation ticket (infra) to add a 30-day TTL to intern service accounts and attach asset-tag metadata; sample onboarding checklist updated. Priority rationale: P2 — not currently blocking hires but medium risk for audit and credential sprawl.
steps_to_reproduce: Example sequence that surfaced the policy gap: 1) Team A checked out loaner laptop L-045 for intern starting 2025-05-01 via ad-hoc Slack request. 2) IT created service account svc-intern-joe with owner tag but no TTL. 3) Intern returned L-045 on 2025-05-22; device was scrubbed but KMS rewrap was not performed. 4) Device was reissued to Team B for new intern; svc-intern-joe remained active for 45 days before being discovered in an access review. Expected: ephemeral credentials tied to device, automated TTL/remediation on return.
logs: n/a — this is a policy/process ticket. Relevant artefacts: asset-inventory audit export (gs://redwood-asset-audits/2025-05/device-checkouts.csv), access-review snapshot (internal SSO CSV attached in Confluence page).

2025-06-15 15:40 - Legal (S. Park): We need a short clause on data subject to retention requirements and confirmation that device wipe meets NIST 800-88 guidelines. Will review draft policy once posted.
2025-06-18 11:03 - Priya Nair: Drafted policy skeleton in Confluence and created infra ticket (GH-4789) for TTL + asset metadata. Requested SRE to validate KMS rewrap procedure.
investigation_notes: Spoke to IT asset manager (J. Lopez). Findings: current pool tracking is a shared Google Sheet with inconsistent fields; KMS keys are per-device model only, not per-asset tag. Short-term options: (A) implement mandatory asset-tag metadata and TTL at SA creation; (B) require a KMS rewrap/rekey step in deprovision checklist; (C) enforce audit gate before device reissue. Constraints: procurement team must label devices first and update the inventory; legal requires wipe verification artifact.
resolution: Draft policy created and posted to Confluence (see related_confluence_pages). Infra ticket GH-4789 opened to add 30-day TTL and asset_tag label to ephemeral service accounts. Next steps: legal review (target 2025-06-25), IT to pilot the process for two upcoming interns in July, and add a mandatory KMS rewrap step to the deprovision runbook. This ticket will remain open until pilot completes and runbook is updated.
